correctness.rationale: The complete dual of the ordinary four-cut complex is defined by forbidding disconnected four-subsets; it has precisely 1887 nonempty faces of dimensions 0–5. The packaged deterministic vertex-toggle matching pairs 925 covers, leaving one critical vertex and 36 critical four-cells, and an exact topological sort of all 7455 directed Hasse covers visits all 1887 nodes. Thus the dual is a wedge of 36 four-spheres. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality gives exactly Z^36 in homology degree eight for the original complex. A separate complete facet enumeration gives its full seven-skeleton; Hurewicz and the simply connected homological Whitehead theorem then prove the original is a wedge of 36 eight-spheres. No homotopy implication rests merely on a numerical Betti experiment.

value.rationale: KG(6,2) is the smallest triangle-containing member of the two-subset Kneser family and the next natural example after the Petersen graph, precisely beyond the triangle-free range highlighted by the owning paper. Its complete ordinary four-cut integral homotopy type is a natural invariant. The nonzero eighth homology two degrees below ten-dimensional facets proves nonshellability, an informative structural obstruction rather than an isolated face count. The classification is meaningful for this exact natural graph without requiring a general-family theorem.
